historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Beta-adrenoceptor blockers

starting.description: Clinical and physiological observations suggested reducing adrenaline-driven cardiac demand. Known endogenous catecholamine effects and the selective agonist isoprenaline supplied the functional/structural clue, followed by informative DCI observations and deliberate antagonist development.

inspiration.description: Clinical angina/adrenaline relationships, cardiac-demand physiology, noradrenaline-related isoprenaline activity, receptor reasoning and DCI findings supplied complementary inspirations. Rational antagonist design is preserved as a contribution.

steps.description: Clinical/physiological problems and adrenergic responses motivated the beta-blockade goal.
The isoprenaline structure was the starting chemical clue for planned agonist-to-antagonist analogue exploration.
DCI findings and improved assays revealed useful antagonist/partial-agonist behavior and motivated pronethalol.
Further deliberate chemistry sought improved safety/activity and produced propranolol, helping establish the class.

design.description: Investigators deliberately sought a new pharmacological action, changing an agonist-related structure into an antagonist and improving the assay, potency and safety. These are substantial design/function changes, not merely delivery modifications, within an observation-inspired programme.

circumstances.description: The project and chemical changes were planned; DCI's tissue-dependent activity and its reassessment supplied a named unexpected contribution.

evidence.locator: Printed p.419, isoprenaline and receptor pharmacology paragraph
Printed pp.420–422, DCI experiments and reassessment
Printed p.424, development from prototype pronethalol

limits: The primary classification uses Ha's broad biological-observation criterion. Black's cold-started search for an antagonist retained explicit clinical/physiological and working-agonist clues.
Agonist-to-antagonist design changed function; it is not described as merely improving delivery or as a natural antagonist isolated unchanged.
The class is the unit; no separate histories of later cohort beta blockers or universal scaffold inheritance are asserted.
gaps: Official Nobel PDF remained403; the relevant original lecture was read through its identified transcript access copy. The copy's typography/OCR is not a substitute for figure-level inspection.
Original Powell/Slater1958 and Black1964 reports were located at metadata extent only, with no abstract/full-text reading claimed.
Stapleton1997 was read at abstract extent; no independent full-class priority adjudication or later-agent biographies were undertaken.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Angina provoked by emotion or adrenaline, thyroidectomy benefit and ineffective coronary vasodilators helped Black formulate beta blockade.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: A synthesis of clinical, physiological and pharmacological evidence, not a single cohort study or exclusively clinical origin.
